Charleston White returns to VladTV for a candid, comedic exchange with DJ Vlad about Royce White’s viral remarks on gender identity, transgender athletes and the WNBA conversation. After praising the former NBA player’s “critical thinking,” Charleston says White’s perspective has him rethinking what it means to identify as a woman, sparking an unexpected FaceTime call between the two.

The conversation touches on the WNBA draft debate, Enes Freedom, TS Madison, Caitlyn Jenner, women’s restrooms, and the broader culture-war discussion around transgender inclusion in sports. Royce White explains his view of gender as a personal journey, while Charleston jokes about wigs, pressure on men, and wanting a “trans confidant” as he works through the idea.

A provocative, offbeat VladTV moment blending humor, social commentary and trending debates around gender, sports and identity.

--------
Royce White sits down with Vlad to address Enes Kanter Freedom’s push to enter the WNBA conversation and the courtside incident that ended with Kanter being escorted out of a Chicago Sky game. White makes clear he and Kanter are not politically aligned, citing differences over Turkey, U.S. foreign policy, the CIA, William Burns, Ilhan Omar, and Uyghur advocacy. He also weighs in on Kanter’s “woman = adult human female” shirt, the confrontation involving Natasha Cloud, and the Sophie Cunningham remark, arguing the ejection and reported suspension were unnecessary. White compares the Chicago reaction to his own Indiana Fever appearance in a wig, saying the Indianapolis crowd was welcoming. The interview also touches on political divides, WNBA culture, LGBTQ and Antifa-related backlash online, and White’s claim that he has faced increased racial abuse since his recent public statements.

recentItems.title: Aryan Brotherhood's Rex Holloway on Gas Station Robbery that Sent Him to Prison at Age 17 (Part 3)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 2: https://youtu.be/PLboJVkKUJo
Part 1: https://youtu.be/ngv3shqEXoM
--------
In this VladTV interview, Rex Holloway reflects on the choices that led him from a troubled Texas adolescence into prison at 17. Holloway describes dropping out of school, living in a “weed house,” selling marijuana and LSD, and getting drawn into robberies around Houston, East Houston, and Missouri City during the early ’90s. He recalls how a late-night gas station robbery with shotguns unraveled when police pulled the crew over with guns and cash hidden in the trunk. Arrested on September 25, 1995, Holloway was charged with two counts of aggravated robbery and ultimately took a 10-year plea. He also discusses Texas law changes during the crack epidemic and “super predator” era that made him ineligible for boot camp because a deadly weapon was involved.

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with Vlad to explain how recruitment into the Mexican Mafia really worked inside California prisons—dispelling myths about being “jumped in” and detailing the sponsorship, voting process, and lifetime commitment behind becoming a made member. Mendoza recalls being accepted on the San Quentin yard, the role of figures like Big Mike and San Diego’s Matt Korean, and how status inside prison gang culture pushed him deeper into violence.

He also discusses his claim that after joining La Eme, he was directly involved in six prison homicides before his 1975 release, describing how repeated violence led to desensitization. The conversation covers prison wars involving Nuestra Familia, the Black Guerrilla Family, and Mendoza’s transfer through Vacaville, Folsom, Soledad, and the California Medical Facility amid the controversial Lister program.

--------

Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee sits down with Vlad to discuss watching Keefe D’s 2019 VladTV appearance and why he was surprised to hear such detailed comments about the Tupac Shakur murder case without clear immunity. The conversation explores Keefe D’s alleged “Queen for a Day” proffer situation, the limits of cooperation agreements, and why public interviews can create serious legal risks. Vlad also recalls paying Keefe D for the interview and hearing that money pressures involving his wife, Paula, may have played a role. Dirt Rocc explains that Keefe D’s version sounded largely accurate compared to what he had heard, but says the later interviews on platforms like Cam Capone and The Dialog became increasingly graphic. He also details being approached by Las Vegas detectives in 2023 as investigators revisited the Tupac case and sought to corroborate information already circulating publicly.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/2-Bi3FMDiz4
--------
Former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving and former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill join Vlad for a candid debate on self-defense, gun rights, and Stand Your Ground laws across Texas, New York, and California. The conversation examines how high-profile cases involving George Zimmerman and Trayvon Martin, Lil Tim, King Von and Quando Rondo, plus the Karmelo Anthony stabbing case, have shaped public views on when force is legally justified.

Irving explains his Texas perspective on protecting family while stressing that violence is not his first option. O’Neill weighs in on deterrence, responsibility, and how culture can change people’s understanding of deadly force. The discussion then turns to a direct firearms question: if they could own only one gun for life, O’Neill chooses a pump-action shotgun for home defense, while Irving picks the AR-15 for its versatility, range, and low recoil.
